title: Impact of Microfinance Branch Entry on Household Consumption

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Difference-in-Differences (DID). This method compares changes in household consumption before and after microfinance branch entry between treated regions (with new branches) and control regions (without new branches). The key assumption is parallel trends: treated and control households would have had similar consumption growth trajectories in the absence of microfinance branch entry.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(broom)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s39_data.csv")

# Main DID regression
did_model <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = data)
did_results <- summary(did_model)
print("=== MAIN DID RESULTS ===")
print(did_results)

# Extract and print the key coefficient
did_effect <- coef(did_model)["treat_x_post"]
did_se <- summary(did_model)$coefficients["treat_x_post", "Std. Error"]
did_pvalue <- summary(did_model)$coefficients["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"]

cat("\n=== KEY FINDING ===\n")
cat(sprintf("DID Effect: %.4f (SE: %.4f, p-value: %.4f)\n", 
            did_effect, did_se, did_pvalue))
cat(sprintf("Interpretation: Microfinance branch entry increases household consumption by %.2f%%\n", 
            (exp(did_effect) - 1) * 100))

# Robustness Check 1: Check parallel trends assumption
# Calculate mean consumption by group and period
trends_data <- data %>%
  group_by(treated, period) %>%
  summarise(mean_y = mean(y), .groups = 'drop')

print("\n=== PARALLEL TRENDS CHECK ===")
print("Mean consumption by treatment status and period:")
print(trends_data)

# Visual parallel trends check
ggplot(trends_data, aes(x = period, y = mean_y, color = factor(treated))) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Parallel Trends Check", 
       x = "Period", y = "Mean Log Consumption",
       color = "Treated") +
  theme_minimal()

# Robustness Check 2: Alternative specification with fixed effects
# Since we have panel data, include unit fixed effects if multiple periods per unit
unit_counts <- data %>% count(unit_id)
if(max(unit_counts$n) > 1) {
  fe_model <- lm(y ~ factor(unit_id) + post + treat_x_post, data = data)
  fe_results <- summary(fe_model)
  fe_effect <- coef(fe_model)["treat_x_post"]
  cat(sprintf("\nRobustness - Fixed Effects Model DID Effect: %.4f\n", fe_effect))
}

# Robustness Check 3: Placebo test (if we have pre-treatment periods)
pre_treatment_data <- data %>% filter(post == 0)
if(nrow(pre_treatment_data) > 0 & length(unique(pre_treatment_data$period)) > 1) {
  # Create a fake treatment indicator for earlier period
  placebo_data <- pre_treatment_data %>%
    mutate(fake_post = ifelse(period == max(period), 1, 0),
           fake_interaction = treated * fake_post)
  
  placebo_model <- lm(y ~ treated + fake_post + fake_interaction, data = placebo_data)
  placebo_effect <- coef(placebo_model)["fake_interaction"]
  placebo_pvalue <- summary(placebo_model)$coefficients["fake_interaction", "Pr(>|t|)"]
  
  cat(sprintf("\nRobustness - Placebo Test Effect: %.4f (p-value: %.4f)\n", 
              placebo_effect, placebo_pvalue))
  cat("Note: Placebo effect should be close to zero and insignificant\n")
}

# Summary statistics by group
cat("\n=== SUMMARY STATISTICS ===\n")
summary_stats <- data %>%
  group_by(treated, post) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_consumption = mean(y),
    sd_consumption = sd(y),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )
print(summary_stats)
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive coefficient on the interaction term (treat_x_post) of approximately 0.10-0.30, indicating that microfinance branch entry increases household consumption by roughly 10-35%. The magnitude reflects typical findings in microfinance literature where access to credit enables households to smooth consumption, invest in income-generating activities, and improve their economic well-being. The effect should be statistically significant (p < 0.05) if microfinance truly impacts household welfare through increased access to financial services.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in household consumption before and after microfinance branch entry between treated and untreated regions.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The entry of a microfinance branch is associated with a positive effect on household consumption.
_ground_truth.main_effect: Approximately 0.15 increase in log household consumption.
